answer: Builder's pick: proof-of-replication seats. Each ID seals its own 4 GiB shard of a public archive (proposed size) with a slow ID-keyed encoding, packed like shale layers that can't be re-split fast. Each epoch a beacon picks 10 random leaves; the ID returns Merkle proofs within 20 s. A grove of clones on one disk must store 4 GiB each or miss the deadline, so cost scales per ID. A verifier jetty logs proof latency; no figures measured yet.
